test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Nisha goes to a shop to purchase a toy drum priced at ₹5,000. She is offered 4 discount options by the shopkeeper. Which of the following options should she opt for to gain maximum advantage of the discount offered?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all into equivalent discount

1) 23% & 23% ⇒ 23 + 23 − (23 × 23)/100 = 46 − 5.29 = 40.71%

2) Single discount = 64%

3) 7% & 45% ⇒ 7 + 45 − (7 × 45)/100 = 52 − 3.15 = 48.85%

4) 10% & 39% ⇒ 10 + 39 − (10 × 39)/100 = 49 − 3.9 = 45.1%

Maximum discount is 64%

**∴ Answer = Option 2 (64% discount)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price = 5000 and four discount options

**Formula used:**

Successive discount = a + b − (ab/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Option 1: Net discount = 23 + 23 − (23 × 23)/100 = 40.71%

⇒ Option 2: Net discount = 64%

⇒ Option 3: Net discount = 7 + 45 − (7 × 45)/100 = 48.85%

⇒ Option 4: Net discount = 10 + 39 − (10 × 39)/100 = 45.1%

⇒ Maximum discount = 64%

**∴ The correct answer is Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

Net discount = a + b − (ab/100)

Comparison Rule

Higher effective discount gives maximum benefit.

Important Insight

Single large discount can sometimes exceed multiple smaller discounts.
